subject: Question about time spent on sampling

messages.author: 7fbbe3361b373823
messages.subject: Question about time spent on sampling
parts:
Hi everyone,
I found the sampling (based on the model I adaped from FS inequity aversion)  took quite a long time: 4 chains, 4 hours each.  My data includes 40 subjects ,114 trials each, that is, totally 5760 records.

i have done the sampling with rstan before on another dataset includes just 1800 records. It took just about 20 minutes.

I wonder what leads to such a long sampling. Is this normal? Does it depends on the complexity of my model and the size of data? Is there some mistakes in my model?

Thanks a lot

Best,
Suiqing

messages.author: 4bcf82a01cf98f56
messages.subject: Re: Question about time spent on sampling
parts:
Hi Suiqing,

Of course, it depends on the model you try, but 4 hours each per chain might not be too bad. And I'm afraid we can only help with models implemented in the hBayesDM. How about posting the model to the Stan mailing list and ask for help?

Thanks,
Young

messages.subject: Re: Question about time spent on sampling
parts:
Hi Young,

Thank you for your suggestion.

I checked the outcome of sampling: convergence is good (no rhat larger than 1.01); y_pred is highly correlated with my behavior data. parameter estimation is as expected.It seems the model itself is well.

I tried running the sampling again and found during this process, CPU use ratio is full but GPU has not been utilized at all. I guess that's where the problems lie. Stan doesn't support GPU acceleration, right? So, do we have some skills that improves the sampling efficiency?

Thanks,
Suiqing

messages.author: 4bcf82a01cf98f56
messages.subject: Re: Question about time spent on sampling
parts:
Hi Suiqing,

I think GPU-based parallel computing in Stan is being discussed, but not sure if it is natively supported in the latest stable Stan release. Please check the Stan mailing list!

Best,
Young
